messages:
Maya: seeing a big tail latency spike during a small burst on `prod-us-west-2` at ~09:03. Warm pool had capacity but new joins took 600-900ms extra and KV lookups show a lot of synchronous priming. Logs point at kernel-selection falling back to scalar kernels which also adds ~200ms per token.
Sam: can you paste the trace id? also which model variant?
Maya: trace=trc_2026_03_18_0903_04, model=vicuna-13b-q4f16 (optimized). I attached the top of the perf profile:
```
# cpu ticks
kv_prefill_sync  42%
kernel_fallback  18%
joiner_wait      12%
batch_aggregation 8%
other            20%
```
Sam: hmm kv_prefill_sync that high is suspicious. Are we priming KV in the join path instead of async background?
Kai: looks like the new batching heuristic change (delta-heuristic v2) pushes more tiny joins through the fast-path but we recently flipped kernel-sensitivity so incompatible blocks trigger fallback. Combined with synchronous priming you get thundering join latency.
Leah: ops-bot alert posted: "autoscale: warm-pool-util spike + join-latency > 400ms". Ops metrics: warm-pool had 8 idle workers, 3 got allocated but spent ~800ms in prefill.
ops-bot: alert_id=ALRT-9876, severity=warning, cpu_pct=82, kv_hitrate=0.24, avg_join_latency=412ms
Sam: mitigation plan: (1) temporarily disable kernel-fallback for this model id (force preferred kernel), (2) shift KV priming to async background priming thread, (3) raise warm-pool.min from 5->8 for the canary region. That should reduce tail while we instrument.
Maya: I can push (1) and (3) with a short canary in us-west-2 now. (2) needs a small runtime change but I can ship a feature-flagged branch.
Kai: small note — forcing preferred kernel removed a small correctness guard. we should only force on models with matching op signatures (i.e., q4f16 fine). I'll add a safety check in the toggles.
Leah: doing the warm-pool bump now.
deploy-bot: started config change: warm_pool.min=8 for target=us-west-2 (canary) by Leah at 09:12
Maya: pushed kernel-fallback toggle for canary, rolled to 10% of canary pool.
deploy-bot: rollout successful to 10% canary at 09:13
Sam: running the priming async branch through unit tests — ETA 2h, but can land behind feature flag and enable gradually.
Leah: metrics after canary change: avg_join_latency down to 160ms, kv_prefill_sync drops to ~6%. Throughput back to expected. :thumbsup:
Maya: nice. we'll keep the kernel-fallback disabled for the canary and monitor for correctness regressions. schedule a deeper postmortem if anything odd shows up.
Kai: follow-ups: add a metric for "kernel-selection-fallback-rate" per model, and a histogram for priming latency. also add a prewarm synthetic priming job for heavy models during scale-up.
Sam: I'll open a short RFC + perf dashboard patch.
Maya: thanks team. tagging @paging oncall if this reappears.
deploy-bot: canary promoted to 100% after 15m with no regressions at 09:28
